order: Complete a blind validation pass against the pre-registered open-item corpus. Record every disagreement that surfaces, and save the independent pass before the sealed corpus file is opened. Grading after the file is unsealed would invalidate the pass, and it must never be accepted as the recorded result. Compare the pass item by item against the reference grading, and report the match rate against the pre-registered threshold. For each disagreement, name the two candidate classes, and state whether it reflects a genuine ambiguity in the border rule or a flaw found in the corpus item itself, flagging the one at the ambiguity cap as genuine while recording it as exactly one ambiguity and nothing more. If the match rate falls short of the threshold, trigger the pre-registered next step, an additional border revision, before the taxonomy counts as validated for downstream encoding.
claims: The independent pass graded seventeen of twenty items, 85 percent, against the pre-registered corpus, missing the threshold required to pass. Three disagreements were recorded in the ledger: one on an evidence-class pair, exactly one flagged as a genuine ambiguity at the ambiguity cap, and one on a diagnosis-class pair, with no flaw found in any corpus item itself. Per the pre-registered rule, the second border pass was triggered before the taxonomy proceeds to downstream encoding.
